trajectory.thought: The leader is the full-pool mean (a baseline/seed), the runner-up (median) is statistically indistinguishable (margin 0.00124), and the diagnosis confirms unstable ranking with high error correlation — conditions where robust full-pool averaging is the right call and further tuning is unlikely to produce a real gain.

action_args.justification: The series has a moderate trend, weak seasonality, and high cross-model error correlation (mean 0.854, only 3 independent groups). Model ranking is unstable across the 3 validation windows (Kendall tau -0.076), so no subset or fitted weighting can be trusted to generalize. The full-pool mean is the simplest robust aggregator, and the median (runner-up) is statistically indistinguishable. Under these conditions — noisy regime, unstable ranking, redundant models — a plain mean over the full pool is the most defensible combination, and the indistinguishable verdict confirms no other strategy is meaningfully better.
